name: ManiSkill2
ability_definition: The ability to quickly move your hand, your hand together with your arm, or your two hands to grasp, manipulate, or assemble objects.

task_realism.reasoning: Tasks such as peg insertion with millimetre-level clearance, plugging in a charger, kit assembly, picking objects and opening cabinets closely resemble real grasp, manipulate and assemble work. They are stripped-down, single-goal versions rather than full workplace procedures, and they use a parallel gripper instead of a hand.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: Evaluation happens entirely in physics simulation. It lacks real sensor noise, real contact dynamics, wear, and the consequences of failure. Randomized object poses and per-episode time limits add some variability and pressure, but the sim-to-real gap is substantial. Speed is not scored beyond the time cutoff.

construct_coverage.reasoning: It covers the core components of grasping, contact-rich manipulation and precise assembly across many object instances, and a few tasks use two arms. It misses multi-finger in-hand dexterity, quickness as a scored dimension, sustained bimanual coordination, and handling deformable or real-world objects at production pace.

format_match.reasoning: Inputs are robot-style observations (RGB-D, point clouds, proprioception) and outputs are continuous low-level control actions, the same kind of interface a real manipulation system uses. It is not an artificial multiple-choice or grid format, though the scenes and objects are simulated assets.

transferability_reasoning: ManiSkill2 tests genuine closed-loop manipulation and precision assembly through a control-level interface, so its tasks and formats are meaningfully related to manual dexterity. Transfer is limited by simulation-only evaluation, a two-finger gripper instead of a dexterous hand, and the lack of any direct measure of speed, which is central to the O*NET definition. Success in the benchmark therefore indicates relevant capability but overstates real-world dexterous performance.

2023.metric: average success rate (%) across the challenge's rigid-body test tasks
2023.human_reference: General adult workforce doing routine manual handling and assembly work, such as assemblers, warehouse and production workers. Their typical level of manual dexterity is the reference.
